== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was born about 1794, calculated from the age of eighty-four reported at his death. The Glasgow family monument at Tamlaght O'Crilly calls him a son of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and Rose.<ref name="Grave">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ ''Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower Graveyard''], transcription of the Adam and Rose Glasgow family monument.</ref>

The leading civil record identifies James as a married farmer of Inishrush who died there on 12 December 1878, reportedly aged eighty-four. Henry Glasgow was present at the death; the register does not state Henry's relationship.<ref name="Death1878">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1878/020497/7192875.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], James Glasgow, Inishrush, 12 December 1878, entry 138; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cide-5928386 database entry].</ref>

The family monument transcribes the death as 11 December, one day earlier than the civil register.<ref name="Grave" /> The two sources concern the same death; the original civil-register date is used for the structured field and the one-day conflict is retained here.

Adam Glasgow's 1833 tithe entry gives a gross area of eleven Irish or Plantation acres, approximately 17.82 statute acres under the National Archives of Ireland's published conversion guidance.<ref name="AdamTithe">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Tamlaght O'Crilly Tithe Applotment Book, PRONI FIN/5/A/254B, image 20, manuscript folio 16, Adam Glasgow at Inishrush; [https://www.nationalarchives.ie/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Family_History_Sources_NAI.pdf National Archives of Ireland, ''Family History Sources''], tithe-acreage guidance.</ref> James later occupied Inishrush plot 29 in the Valuation Revision Books, but the similar acreages and later occupancy are evidence of a property sequence, not a stated inheritance or proof that every James entry concerns this profile.<ref name="Valuation">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Valuation Revision Books, Inishrush plot 29, VAL/12/B/34/10A–10D; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/Val12B/Search.aspx PRONI Valuation Revision Books search].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3902]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The Adam and Rose family monument identifies James as their son; his Inishrush death in December 1878 aged about 84 fits James born c 1794. The maintained findings distinguish him from the younger James born c 1813 who married in 1851.

Confident for the older monument James. The 11/12 December date variation is separate from paternity, and the younger man’s marriage is not used as proof.

Next useful test: Compare the monument image for the precise death day, preserving the two James identities.

Source basis already held: [https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ “Tamlaght O’Crilly Lower Graveyard,” One Irish Rover, Glasgow family gravestone (https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Current evidence assessment ===

==== The two James identities ====
An original 1851 marriage records another—or possibly the same—James Glasgow as a 38-year-old bachelor farmer of Inishrush, son of Adam Glasgow. He married Rosanna Barkley, daughter of Henry Barkley.<ref name="Marriage1851">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cima-3208068 IrishGenealogy.ie], marriage of James Glasgow and Rosanna Barkley, 17 March 1851.</ref> A man aged 38 in 1851 would have been about 65 or 66 in 1878, not 84. The records agree on name, father's name, occupation and locality but conflict by about nineteen years in age.

This profile represents the monument-defined son of Adam and Rose and the age-84 death. [[Glasgow-1623|James Glasgow]], the 1851 groom, remains a separate working profile while the one-man and two-man explanations are tested. The existing records do not justify merging them or creating two independently proved fathers named Adam.

==== Unproved associates ====
Henry Glasgow must not be attached as James's son merely because he informed the death. The later valuation sequence from James to Rose Anne and then Adam shows occupancy succession at Inishrush plot 29, not inheritance or kinship.

A 20 March 1847 family letter reported that a James Glasgow had a child by a servant who was a daughter of Henry Barkly.<ref name="Letter1847">[https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/documents/John%20Glasgow%20letter%20to%20Jane%20Glasgow%20Gray%203-20-1847.pdf John Glasgow to Jane Glasgow Gray], 20 March 1847.</ref> The 1851 James-and-Rosanna marriage is the closer documentary match. The letter does not name or sex the child, and the child should not be attached to this older James.

First Kilrea Presbyterian's 1828 register identifies Jane Barklie, daughter of Henry Barkly and Jane Galloway, marrying Peter Aikin. Henry's 1831 Tyanee household contained four females. This establishes a Barkly household in the relevant locality, but it does not identify Jane—or any particular daughter—as the servant in the letter.<ref name="BarklyContext">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/KilreaP1/Marriages/1828.html First Kilrea Presbyterian marriage transcription], Peter Aikin and Jane Barklie, 1828; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census_3.html Tamlaght O'Crilly 1831 census transcription], Henry Barkley at Tyanee; and [https://www.billmacafee.com/1831census/1831derrycensusnames.pdf William Macafee, ''Names of Householders Listed in the 1831 Census Returns for the County of Londonderry''].</ref>

Second Portglenone baptisms survive for 1845–49 under PRONI MIC1P/357, but the relevant pages have not been inspected. First Kilrea session minutes, PRONI MIC1P/87 (1825–1852), and Drimbolg Reformed Presbyterian session minutes, PRONI MIC1C/15 (1809–1859), are separate possible discipline-record targets. No negative conclusion should be drawn before those records are searched.<ref name="ChurchGuide">[https://www.billmacafee.com/churchrecords/churchrecordsderry.pdf William Macafee, ''Church Records for County Londonderry''], register and session-book coverage.</ref>

=== Birth ===

James's approximate birth year of 1794 is calculated from the age of 84 recorded at his death in December 1878.

No contemporary baptism or birth record has yet been identified.

=== Parents ===

The Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower family gravestone explicitly identifies James as a son of Adam and Rose Glasgow.<ref name="Gravestone">“Tamlaght O’Crilly Lower Graveyard,” ''One Irish Rover'', [https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ Glasgow family gravestone].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

James's civil death registration records his marital condition as '''married'''.<ref name="JamesDeath">“Civil Records,” database with images, ''Irish Genealogy'', death of James Glasgow, 12 December 1878, Group Registration ID 5928386, Magherafelt registration district, [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cide-5928386 indexed record] and [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1878/020497/7192875.pdf original civil return].</ref>

His wife's identity has not yet been established from the records cited on this profile.

Rose Anne Glasgow should not be identified as his wife merely because she followed him as occupier of plot 29. She belonged to the family of the younger James Glasgow and was that James's widow.

=== Death date ===

The original civil death return records James's death at Inishrush on '''12 December 1878'''. The death was registered on 23 December 1878 by Henry Glasgow, who was present at the death.<ref name="JamesDeath" />

The family gravestone instead records '''11 December 1878'''.<ref name="Gravestone" />

Both sources agree that James died in December 1878 aged 84. The profile uses the date recorded in the civil return while preserving the one-day discrepancy.

=== Henry Glasgow ===

Henry Glasgow is attached as an '''uncertain''' son of James.

The 1878 civil death registration places Henry at Inishrush and records him as the person present at James's death. It does not describe Henry as James's son or state any other family relationship.<ref name="JamesDeath" />

Their shared surname, residence and Henry's presence at the death are consistent with a close family relationship, but the death return alone does not prove parentage.

=== Farm continuity ===

Adam Glasgow's 1833 tithe holding measured 11 Irish or Plantation acres, approximately 17.82 statute acres. James's later valuation plot 29 measured 19 acres 2 roods 10 perches, or 19.5625 statute acres.

The difference is only 1.7425 statute acres, approximately 9.8 per cent. Together with the proved father-son relationship and continued residence at Inishrush, this strongly supports James having succeeded to substantially the same family farm.

It does not establish exact parcel identity. The tithe entry has no map reference linking it directly to valuation plot 29, and the tithe and valuation surveys were made several decades apart for different purposes.

=== Younger James Glasgow, Rosanna Barkley and plot 29 ===

Later Inishrush records involve another [[Glasgow-1623|James Glasgow]], treated in the current family reconstruction as this James's nephew.

A letter written by [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] on 20 March 1847 reported news from Ireland that a James Glasgow had fathered an illegitimate child by a daughter of Henry Barkly.<ref name="JohnLetter">John Glasgow, letter to Jane Glasgow Gray, 20 March 1847, [https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/documents/John%20Glasgow%20letter%20to%20Jane%20Glasgow%20Gray%203-20-1847.pdf digital image].</ref>

The report should not be assigned to this older James. On 17 March 1851 the younger James Glasgow, a 38-year-old bachelor farmer of Inishrush and son of Adam Glasgow, married '''Rosanna Barkley''', a farm servant of Tyanee and daughter of Henry Barkley.<ref name="JamesBarkleyMarriage">“Civil Records,” marriage of James Glasgow and Rosanna Barkley, 17 March 1851, original civil marriage return.</ref>

The combination of the names, Rosanna's father, her servant status and the Inishrush–Tyanee locality makes the younger James and Rosanna the much stronger identification for the couple described in the 1847 letter. The reported child remains unidentified.

Rose Anne Glasgow later succeeded the older James as occupier of Inishrush plot 29, with an 1884 valuation annotation. She was the widow of the younger James, not the wife of this older James. Her succession in the valuation should therefore not be interpreted as a widow inheriting directly from this James.

A later Adam Glasgow replaced Rose Anne as occupier with an 1893 annotation.<ref name="Valuation" /> The valuation entries establish succession in occupation of the farm but do not themselves state the family relationships among the occupants.

Accordingly, neither the 1847 Barkley report nor Rose Anne's succession to plot 29 provides evidence identifying this older James's wife or children.

=== Further research ===

Useful records for this James include:

* records identifying his wife;
* marriage or church records establishing his marriage;
* records explicitly identifying Henry Glasgow's parents;
* estate, lease and valuation material clarifying transmission of the Inishrush farm;
* records identifying the relationships among the later occupants of plot 29.

Research into the child reported in the 1847 Barkley letter belongs primarily with the younger [[Glasgow-1623|James Glasgow]] and Rosanna Barkley rather than with this profile.

First Kilrea Presbyterian session minutes survive for 1825–1852 under PRONI reference ''MIC1P/87'', and the Drimbolg Reformed Presbyterian session or discipline book survives for 1809–1859 under ''MIC1C/15''. Both cover the period of the reported 1846 event and remain relevant unread sources for the younger James and Barkley research.

The death of James Glasgow was registered on 12 December 1878 in Magherafelt, aged 84.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], James Glasgow, 12 December 1878, aged 84, Magherafelt registration district, D/1878/179/1022/7/138.</ref>
